{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Each user story is treated as an independent feature/investigation increment, since the stories span multiple distinct Spring ecosystem projects (Spring XD, Spring Cloud Data Flow, Spring Cloud Stream).",
    "Reuse existing Spring XD composed-job and Spring Cloud Data Flow shell module-discovery infrastructure rather than building new frameworks from scratch.",
    "For U3 and U4 (investigation/spike stories), the deliverable is a written report plus a small reference prototype, not production code.",
    "For U5, dot-delimited property resolution is implemented as a SpEL/PathMapper-style parser layer above the existing property-binding code in Spring Cloud Stream.",
    "For U6, tab completion is implemented using the standard JLine completion API already exposed by the s-c-d shell.",
    "For U7, Mesos deployment leverages the Marathon framework and the existing s-c-d local-server distribution; a new deployer module and Marathon JSON descriptor are produced.",
    "For U8, the redis @Rule and supporting fixtures are extracted into a new Maven/Gradle module published to a separate repository; consuming projects depend on it via test-scope.",
    "Backend (Java/Spring) and front-end (Angular/Fluent UI for s-c-d; XD UI for U1/U2) work is sequenced per story."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all work; estimates are in 8-hour workdays.",
    "Development environment, CI server, Kafka 0.9 broker, and a Mesos/Marathon cluster are available and pre-provisioned.",
    "The XD composed-job runtime already tracks child job execution; only aggregation and persistence layers need to be added.",
    "Existing s-c-d shell commands and module metadata are sufficient to derive tab-completion candidates.",
    "Spring Cloud Stream's property-binding code is open to extension points for the new dot-delimited resolver.",
    "Mesos deployment is targeted at Marathon; DC/OS-specific concerns are out of scope.",
    "The new repo for the redis @Rule starts empty and is owned by the same team; no external coordination overhead.",
    "No major cross-project refactoring, performance tuning, or production rollout is included beyond the listed stories.",
    "Unit and integration tests are written alongside each feature; no dedicated hardening pass beyond the cross-feature integration activity.",
    "All estimates are most-likely (not pessimistic) values."

      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Aggregated progress bar for composed jobs (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Aggregate child job step/percentage progress in the XD composed-job runtime, expose it through the job execution API, render a single progress bar in the XD UI, and cover with unit/integration tests.",

      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Restart capability for composed jobs (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Persist composed-job definition and last-known child state, add a restart REST endpoint and XD shell command, expose a restart control in the UI, and add tests covering relaunch from terminal and intermediate states.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Kafka 0.9 integration investigation (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Spike to integrate the s-c-d message bus bindings with Kafka 0.9, identify API/broker compatibility issues, prototype a working channel, and produce a written findings/improvements report.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Lattice bare-metal bootstrap investigation (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Explore options to bootstrap a Lattice cluster on bare metal, prototype a minimal Terraform/Ansible-based installer for s-c-d, and document recommended approach with pros/cons.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Dot-delimited property resolution for stream definitions (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a property-path parser in Spring Cloud Stream that resolves dot-delimited keys for both Tuple and JSON payloads, integrate with the existing binder, and add unit tests for edge cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Shell tab completion for s-c-d modules and options (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Wire JLine completion into the s-c-d shell, discover available modules and their options at runtime, provide contextual completion for module/option/option-value positions, and add shell-script tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Mesos deployment support for s-c-d (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Design a Marathon-based deployment topology, implement a deployer that generates Marathon JSON descriptors, package the s-c-d server for the cluster, and validate end-to-end deployment on a Mesos/Marathon cluster.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Extract redis @Rule to a separate repository (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Create a new repository/module containing the redis JUnit @Rule and its test fixtures, set up build and publishing configuration, update s-c-d to depend on it via test scope, and verify all consuming tests still pass.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration testing and bug fixing",
      "activity_description": "Run end-to-end integration tests combining the new features (e.g., composed jobs with new shell completion, s-c-d deployed on Mesos), triage failures, and apply fixes that span more than one activity.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Documentation updates",
      "activity_description": "Update reference documentation, user guides, and release notes for the composed-job improvements, dot-delimited property syntax, shell tab completion, Mesos deployment, and the new redis test-fixtures repository.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2.0
    }

technical_and_design_decisions: Each user story is treated as an independent feature/investigation increment, since the stories span multiple distinct Spring ecosystem projects (Spring XD, Spring Cloud Data Flow, Spring Cloud Stream).
Reuse existing Spring XD composed-job and Spring Cloud Data Flow shell module-discovery infrastructure rather than building new frameworks from scratch.
For U3 and U4 (investigation/spike stories), the deliverable is a written report plus a small reference prototype, not production code.
For U5, dot-delimited property resolution is implemented as a SpEL/PathMapper-style parser layer above the existing property-binding code in Spring Cloud Stream.
For U6, tab completion is implemented using the standard JLine completion API already exposed by the s-c-d shell.
For U7, Mesos deployment leverages the Marathon framework and the existing s-c-d local-server distribution; a new deployer module and Marathon JSON descriptor are produced.
For U8, the redis @Rule and supporting fixtures are extracted into a new Maven/Gradle module published to a separate repository; consuming projects depend on it via test-scope.
Backend (Java/Spring) and front-end (Angular/Fluent UI for s-c-d; XD UI for U1/U2) work is sequenced per story.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all work; estimates are in 8-hour workdays.
Development environment, CI server, Kafka 0.9 broker, and a Mesos/Marathon cluster are available and pre-provisioned.
The XD composed-job runtime already tracks child job execution; only aggregation and persistence layers need to be added.
Existing s-c-d shell commands and module metadata are sufficient to derive tab-completion candidates.
Spring Cloud Stream's property-binding code is open to extension points for the new dot-delimited resolver.
Mesos deployment is targeted at Marathon; DC/OS-specific concerns are out of scope.
The new repo for the redis @Rule starts empty and is owned by the same team; no external coordination overhead.
No major cross-project refactoring, performance tuning, or production rollout is included beyond the listed stories.
Unit and integration tests are written alongside each feature; no dedicated hardening pass beyond the cross-feature integration activity.
All estimates are most-likely (not pessimistic) values.
